acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: It’s mid-October, 2013. Freddie Hoyt tries to rally his sales staff to sell 129 cars and trucks by the end of the month. Freddie’s the General Manager at Town and Country Jeep Chrysler Dodge Ram in Levittown, NY, on Long Island. Problem is, the customers are not cooperating. (7 1/2 minutes)

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: How we found this car dealer.

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: A quick primer of who’s who, and how the place works.

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Salesman Bob Tantillo has the fewest sales of anyone at Town and Country this month. Robyn Semien spoke to him.

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Salesman Jason Mascia has the most sales of anyone this month, as usual. Sean Cole spent a week with him watching how he does it.

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: The next-to-last day of the month. Deals fall apart, but not all of them.

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: The last day of the month begins. They have to sell nine cars by the end of the day. "God help us," Freddie says.

acts.label: Act Seven
acts.desc: Joe Monti’s real name is Joe Montalbano. But when he started in the car business, he didn't want to lose a sale because a customer couldn’t keep his name straight so he simplified it for the job. He's one of the managers of the used cars department at Town and Country. Sarah Koenig reports on what it'll mean if he doesn’t make this month’s goal.

acts.label: Act Eight
acts.desc: The last day of the month continues and the truism is accurate: some people get great deals because it’s the end of the month and they have to hit their goal. When you look at the numbers, the average car they sell in the last two days actually loses money.

acts.label: Act Nine
acts.desc: Salesman Manny Rosales keeps to himself in the showroom, with his own sales philosophy. He explained it to Brian Reed.

acts.label: Act Ten
acts.desc: The last day of the month ends.
